questions.ask: What is your date of birth?
What is the postcode of your home address?

intents.hardship: Financial hardship (illness, bereavement, job loss): one sentence of sympathy, then transfer to the Customer Care queue.
intents.dispute: A dispute on a product ("not mine", "closed years ago"): do not argue; note the product N-DISP and continue with the others.
intents.already_paid: "Already paid" on a product: payments can take a business day to show; note the product N-PAID and continue with the others.
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or reduced payments: transfer to the restructuring queue.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much: not a refusal, uses no attempt; offer the same step again with the floor in place of the full arrears.
intents.human: A request for a person: ask once whether you can help; if they insist, transfer to the general queue.

lines.opening: Hello, this is the automated assistant calling from Brackenridge Finance.
lines.robot: Yes, I am an automated assistant calling for Brackenridge Finance.

lines.id_explain: I can only explain why I'm calling once I've checked who I'm speaking with.

lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full overdue amount on all of them today?

lines.date_past: That date has already passed. Could you choose today or a later date?
lines.not_business_day: That isn't a business day. The next business day is {date}. Would that work for you?
lines.after_deadline: The latest date I can accept is {date}. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day could you pay?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.repeat_offer: Coming back to your {name}, could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.readback_intro: Let me read back what we agreed.
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can accept is {date}, so that payment is set for {date}.
lines.recorded: Thank you, your payment promise has been recorded.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, the payment for your {name} could not be recorded because of a system problem.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take a business day to show on your account.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't ask you about this one any further.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that. I'll put you through to our Customer Care team, who can help.
lines.restructure_line: I'll put you through to our restructuring team, who can talk to you about a payment plan.
lines.human_ask_help: Could I help you with it myself?
lines.transfer: Please hold while I transfer you.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change a payment promise that's already in place on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't accept less than {amount}.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer didn't go through.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book the callback.

unsupported_rules: 7.11(c) Financial hardship (illness, bereavement, job loss): one sentence of sympathy, then transfer to the Customer Care queue. Do not ask further questions.
CO-26-15 item 3: For calls closed from 2 November 2026, the outcome code PAID is replaced by CLAIMED_PAID. The ledger rejects PAID from that date.
assumptions: Read the documents in date order: Hamish's email (20 Oct) is corrected by Priya's (22 Oct); CO-26-14 (21 Oct) is corrected by CO-26-15 (28 Oct).
Wrong answers: Priya overrides Hamish's limit of two. The third wrong answer, on either question, ends the check, so max_wrong = 3 counted in total.

Card floor: Priya overrides Hamish. It is 12% of arrears_gbp, rounded up to the next multiple of £5 (an exact multiple of £5 stays as it is), then raised to at least £25 after rounding, then capped at the arrears. Examples: £437.80 -> 52.536 -> £55; £150 -> 18 -> 20 -> £25; £20 -> 2.40 -> 5 -> 25 -> capped at £20; £250 -> 30 -> £30.

Callback window: Monday to Thursday 09:00-20:00 (Hamish's hours, which Priya confirmed); Friday 09:00-16:00 (Priya's correction of 17:00). Both ends included. Callbacks are only today or the next business day and never earlier than now. Weekends have no callbacks, and holidays are excluded because only business days are allowed.
Holidays: the policy's list plus 2026-11-27 from CO-26-14. 2026-12-07 was added by CO-26-14 but withdrawn by CO-26-15, so it is a business day.
MOTOR band 2 deadline is the 3rd business day after today (CO-26-14 item 1, confirmed by CO-26-15 item 2). Attempts are unchanged.
MOTOR band 3 floor is the full arrears (7.5c). The MOTOR floor is named 'minimum payment' so that the band 3 floor is not called a contractual monthly payment.
PAID is replaced by CLAIMED_PAID for calls closed from 2 November 2026 (CO-26-15 item 3). The build is used after the memo dates, so CLAIMED_PAID is used for the paid event.
The dispute note is N-DISP. N-DSP is deprecated.

Hardship: the brief transfers straight to Q-VULN with no offer, and N-HARD is for human agents only. The hardship event therefore uses XFER/CARE with no note, and on any transfer no notes are written (7.11f).
create_promise failures are never retried (promise_retries = 0). The product is noted N-SYS and the call carries on as normal.
get_account amounts are in pounds with pence; create_promise takes integer pence, so promise_scale = 100. The brief gives no rounding rule because the amounts are already in pence.
Date of birth is sent as DDMMYYYY (%d%m%Y), and numeric dates are read day-month-year. The postcode is sent in capitals with no spaces, and no fixed length is set because UK postcodes vary in length.
The verify_identity response has no hint field, so hints are empty.
Step 1 uses full_or_floor because, after 'too much', every step uses the floor in place of the full arrears (7.8). Step 2 then repeats step 1 and is skipped without using an attempt (7.7).
'Too much' said to the opening ask: each product starts at step 1 with the floor (too_much_floor = attempt_1).
If today is the last business day of this week, steps 1 and 2 use the last business day of next week (week_end_today = next_week). A step date after the product's deadline uses the deadline.
customer_ref is mapped to the customer_id call variable in every tool body.

The brief is silent on these, so defaults are used: date_rules.next_weekday = following_week, callback.max_asks = 2, max_not_talk = 2, after_promise.ask_anything_else = true, purpose_is_decline = true, deadline_adjust = previous_business_day (computed deadlines are already business days).
The brief gives no rule for changing a promise that is already recorded, so the agent says it cannot be changed on this call. The brief requires no SMS sentence.
